The dword/word read at 0x4adb28 both include that byte as the lowest-addressed (low) byte, and the very next instruction 0x4adb2b does and ecx,0xff, which discards every other byte. So ecx after 0x4adb2b (and the flags set by it and by test at 0x4adb31) is the same for RD32 and RD16, whatever the other bytes of [ebp-4] hold.

test ecx,ecx at 0x4adb31 computes ecx & ecx; the mutant computes ecx | ecx. Both operands are the same register, so both results equal ecx and FL41_LOGIC derives identical flags (cf=of=0, zf, sf, pf from the same value). Nothing else differs.

The instruction before it, and ecx,0xff at 0x4adb2b, already set zf/sf/pf from the result now in ecx and clear cf/of; test ecx,ecx at 0x4adb31 computes ecx&ecx = ecx with ecx unchanged in between, so it sets exactly the same flags. The only consumer is jne at 0x4adb33 (zf); later flag users 0x4adb3a and 0x4adb48 overwrite flags first. Dropping it changes nothing.

Flags at 0x4adb33 come from test ecx,ecx at 0x4adb31 where ecx = x & 0xff (0x4adb2b), so ecx <= 0xff: sf = bit31 = 0 and test clears of, hence sf == of always holds. The mutant condition (!zf && sf==of) therefore equals !zf, the original.

At 0x4adb3a the new low byte of edx is r = (dl & 0x7f). The mutant additionally preserves bit 0 of the old edx via mask 0xffffff01. Bit 0 of r equals bit 0 of dl (0x7f has bit 0 set), so OR-ing old bit 0 into the result changes nothing in the low byte; bits 1..7 and the upper 24 bits are identical. edx is only used as dl at the store 0x4adb3d and then never read again before the return.

Slot [ebp-4] has its low byte written by the byte store at 0x4adb3d. The read at 0x4adb40 (32-bit vs 16-bit) both contain that byte as the low byte, and 0x4adb43 does and eax,0xff, which discards the rest; the cmp at 0x4adb48 and everything after use only the low byte. So eax and the flags are identical.
